summary.answer: Source-visible answer: the post-phase requirement resolver. Ordering facts: (1) it asserts the function's preinit already completed (predone) or the system is ignore-flagged - post execution presupposes pre phase completion; (2) it walks reqs and thread-spawns exec_post_system for each required system without waiting; (3) array form asserts each requirement value is defined, not registry-entry existence; a defined absent name spawns exec_post_system(undefined), which returns at37-39. Only scalar form asserts registry-entry existence at75. Because both the array and single-req paths spawn and return, the requirement/dependent postinit ordering is scheduler-dependent, not synchronized - pre-phase completeness is asserted, with original VM assertion behavior still unknown. exec_post_system skips calls that observe ignore or postdone. It checks postdone before requirement resolution, then sets postdone after that resolution and before postfunc. There is no second postdone check after resolution, so once-only behavior across invocations admitted before the mark and unproved interleavings is not established. HMH linkage: this is the shared dependency-scheduling core the six HMH root candidates participate in via the registry; wz-side registries (e.g. hash_280fe2667ed2d300 reqs #item_supply_drop, script_71e26f08f03b7a7a.gsc 12-15; killstreak req chains supplydrop.gsc 44/uav.gsc 28) route through exactly this code. Missing native original-build facts are listed in native_gaps.
summary.behavior: Post requirement resolver. function_5095b2c6(func): first asserts func.predone || func.ignore (dev string x8d) (60) - a post phase may only be driven for systems whose preinit completed or which are ignored, otherwise it is an assert boundary; if func.reqs defined: array case asserts each req defined and spawns thread exec_post_system(level.system_funcs[req]) per element then returns (64-72); scalar case asserts isdefined(level.system_funcs[reqs]) (75, with ishash/hashtostring dev rendering) and spawns thread exec_post_system for it (76). No waiting on the spawned requirements - dependency scheduling is asynchronous spawn, and each spawned exec_post_system re-checks !defined/ignore/postdone (37-42) before resolving its own requirements. It sets postdone after requirement resolution and before its postfunc call; suppression is supported for calls observing the mark, while once-only execution across earlier admitted invocations remains unproved. Called from exec_post_system (46) and run_post_systems (88) only; corpus search shows no other callers. Both VM twins carry identical code (csc/gsc 58-78).

summary.answer: Source-visible answer: registration is state-only (no invocation); when an existing record has ignore=1, every repeated register call asserts that ignore flag and returns without clearing it; the record may be a placeholder or a previously real record marked by ignore (register assert only on .ignore, csc 11-15; ignore() sets ignore=1, csc 169-179). Ordering graph produced (see source_trace): autoexec __init__system__ -> register -> native level_preinit -> codecallback_preinitialization -> run_pre_systems -> exec_pre_system per entry; native level_finalizeinit -> codecallback_finalizeinitialization -> run_post_systems -> exec_post_system per entry -> set system_init_complete -> registry cleared -> on_finalize_initialization dispatch. Dependency waits: NONE - req-resolution spawns threads without joining (69/76), the only synchronization is the whole-batch flag "system_init_complete" (92) consumed by wait_till (162). Error behavior: all failures are assert() with dev strings; retail evaluation of assert is a native/build fact. HMH root/registrant linkage: the HMH map script wz_open_skyscrapers.gsc::main joins this mechanism by load::main -> system::wait_till("all") (wz_open_skyscrapers.gsc 53; load.gsc 35) and by callback::on_finalize_initialization registration (47) delivered inside codecallback_finalizeinitialization after run_post_systems; the mechanism therefore conditions the whole HMH map startup; the exact set of registrant systems loaded into the HMH server VM is the unresolved native bundle boundary (m1 unknowns #1).
summary.behavior: Registration store for the per-VM system registry; server file lines 9-29 and client twin lines 9-29 are textually identical at this revision. register(str_name, func_preinit, func_postinit, reqs): if level.system_funcs[str_name] already exists it asserts the existing record's .ignore and returns WITHOUT replacing the stored prefunc/postfunc/reqs (csc/gsc 11-15) - repeated regular registration is an assert boundary; any existing ignore-flagged record, including a real record later marked by ignore, permits repeated early returns; ignore remains set. Otherwise it lazily creates level.system_funcs, stores a spawnstruct with prefunc/postfunc/reqs and initializes predone=!isdefined(func_preinit), postdone=!isdefined(func_postinit), ignore=0 (17-28). No execution happens here; the record is pure state consumed by exec_pre/exec_post_system. The following are named source registration witnesses, not a corpus-wide count or proof of the actual retail HMH registrant set; conditional server-source examples: mp_common/callbacks.gsc autoexec __init__system__ registers "callback" preinit &__init__ (23-26) whose preinit installs level.callbackplayerconnect etc. via set_default_callbacks (65-98); util_shared.gsc registers "util_shared" pre &__init__ post &__main__ (21-24); the four hashed systems #using-imported by wz_open_skyscrapers.gsc register hash_18ce058ad321248f (script_34e49e82e2f499e1.gsc 13-16), hash_32ef71953f1186eb (script_5f3e7d348fbc5283.gsc 10-13), hash_280fe2667ed2d300 with reqs #"item_supply_drop" (script_71e26f08f03b7a7a.gsc 12-15), hash_502d65acd9829223 (script_7611295950bc2c87.gsc 10-13); killstreak systems that wz later ignores register with reqs (killstreaks/mp/supplydrop.gsc 44 and uav.gsc 28, req #"killstreaks").
